library_name: MotifAI Master Composition & Performance Palette Archive
purpose: A curated archive of flexible musical architecture seeds, instrument-role palettes, production principles, and documented Strudel visual-feedback options. The archive is broad; each generation request receives only one selected architecture and a small relevant selection of palette guidance.

selection_policy.ordinary_request_behavior: Auto-select one best-fit architecture seed for each request, including evolution, unless the user opts out. This is guidance, not fixed source code or an obligatory song form.
selection_policy.retry_behavior: Choose once before the generation retry loop. Inject the same single delimited guidance block once into each fresh attempt prompt. Never append blocks to a growing conversation or reselect during technical repair.
selection_policy.evolution_behavior: The same selector runs for creation and evolution. For evolution, interpret the selected seed as an optional development lens around the existing score; do not replace the user's material wholesale unless requested.
selection_policy.smart_palette_budget: Inject the selected architecture, 2-5 matching instrument-role cards, 1-3 production principles, and 1-3 relevant visual cards. Expand palette count only for an explicit request for detailed/full visual or orchestration guidance.
selection_policy.nonnegotiable: User intent and MotifAI's pinned embedded Strudel runtime contract override the archive. Documentation status is not evidence of embedded availability or audible playback. Never assume a sample, synth preset, UI slider, visualizer hook, Hydra integration, or arrangement helper is enabled without runtime evidence.
selection_policy.ctrl_p_note: Ctrl+P opens the TUI archive picker: AUTO chooses one best-fit blueprint per request, FREE-FORM turns injection off, and choosing an ID pins that blueprint for creation and evolution. All 65 blueprint IDs also remain addressable through MOTIFAI_COMPOSITION_BLUEPRINT=<id> or blueprint:<id> in a prompt.

visual_runtime_policy.default_approach: Inline visual feedback only when it helps the piece or the user asked for visuals. Choose visualizers by data type: event timing, pitch-time, waveform, spectrum, cycle, or pitch-class. Never attach every visual to every instrument.
visual_runtime_policy.notation_feedback: .color(...) supports mini-notation color/highlighting; it does not affect audio.
visual_runtime_policy.extension_only: Hydra-based visuals are explicitly marked extension-only. Do not initialize Hydra unless the user asks for it and the host/runtime is confirmed compatible.
visual_runtime_policy.per_instrument_mapping: Every instrument-role card maps to suitable visual_palette_ids, but only representative stems should be visualized to avoid editor clutter.

arc.transition_intent: Reduce or resolve energy rather than adding layers without purpose.

A return that relates to the opening

If the user asks for a completely through-composed piece, do not force a literal return.
blueprints.duration_guidance: Scale the number and length of stages to the request; do not assign fixed bars unless requested.

blueprints.name: Tension and Release Club Arc

arc.intent: Introduce a sparse motif or narrow interval with little rhythmic certainty.
arc.transition_intent: Let silence or gap length become meaningful.

arc.intent: Add one rhythmic or spectral layer without resolving the unease.
arc.transition_intent: Break the regularity before it becomes comfortable.

arc.intent: Temporarily reveal a more consonant or stable version of the motif.
arc.transition_intent: Invert or fragment the signpost after the calm.

arc.intent: Return the motif distorted by changed register/rhythm/timbre, then reduce to a final residue.
arc.transition_intent: Avoid relying on a named horror sample library.

escape_conditions: Dissonance is intentional only when it serves the brief; no unverified effect is required.
blueprints.duration_guidance: Extended score; restrained event count.

blueprints.name: Joyful Broken-Beat Future Soul
blueprints.premise: Combine warm harmonic movement with a playful broken-beat pocket and a lead motif that sounds like a conversation with the drums.

arc.intent: Introduce a colorful chord or melodic gesture over light percussion.
arc.transition_intent: Give the bass a responsive rhythm.

arc.intent: Expand the groove with complementary high percussion and a short melodic answer.
arc.transition_intent: Reduce the groove to bass and one accent briefly.

arc.intent: Bring back the theme with fuller harmony or altered rhythmic placement.
arc.transition_intent: End with a bright but uncluttered final gesture.

escape_conditions: Do not force a specific scale or sample set just because a genre is referenced.
blueprints.duration_guidance: Medium; should feel supple rather than overbuilt.

instrument_palettes.name: Kick / Pulse Foundation
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Anchor the pulse and define the weight of the groove. Leave spectral and rhythmic room for bass; the kick does not need to hit every subdivision.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Start from the documented default-map kick sample `bd` when a sample drum is appropriate. Shape placement, rests, accents, velocity/gain, and contrast before adding extra effects. Avoid assuming custom kick banks exist.
arrangement_moves: hold the kick steady while surrounding layers evolve
remove it before a drop or expose it alone
use sparse kick punctuation in ambient or broken-beat contexts
instrument_palettes.compatibility: `bd` is a documented common default-map abbreviation; verify active sound map and lazy loading in the target REPL.

instrument_palettes.name: Snare / Clap / Backbeat
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Give the groove a recognizable backbeat, response, or accent identity. A snare and clap can reinforce one event, but avoid stacking them at excessive gain by default.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use documented common-map names such as `sd` or `cp` only when present in the active map; let rhythm and event placement do most of the work.
arrangement_moves: alternate snare and clap response
remove the backbeat for a breakdown
change accent placement while preserving the core pulse
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Sample-map dependent even for common aliases; confirm in the embedded REPL.

instrument_palettes.name: Hi-Hats / Cymbals / Metallic Percussion
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Provide subdivision, motion, brightness, and phrase articulation. Change density or openness intentionally; use rests to prevent high-frequency fatigue.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Prefer common-map `hh`, `oh`, `rd`, or `cr` when available. Avoid assuming every bank has every abbreviation. Use filtering carefully and don't create a wall of hats on every beat division.
arrangement_moves: vary subdivision between sections
open the high end in the build and reduce it at impact
use one short cymbal event to mark a transition
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Default sample map has common percussion aliases but exact variants are map-dependent.

instrument_palettes.name: Hand Percussion / World-Rhythm Colors
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create interlocking rhythmic voices and call-and-response, not an undifferentiated layer of random percussion. Keep the pulse legible beneath the interlock.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use only percussion samples confirmed in the sound browser; when uncertain, build the rhythm from known `perc`, `rim`, `cb`, or `tb` aliases if present, and keep any bank optional.
arrangement_moves: trade short rhythmic phrases between two registers
thin to one voice before the ensemble returns
make accent cycles differ without losing a shared pulse
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Specific conga/bongo/world sample names are not guaranteed by the default map.

instrument_palettes.name: Sub-Bass Anchor
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Supply controlled low-frequency weight and reinforce kick rhythm without obscuring it. Use sparse note movement, deliberate duration, and restrained gain.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: A documented oscillator source such as `sine` or `triangle` can be a safe synth baseline when supported. Use low-register note patterns and `lpf(...)` as appropriate. Do not confuse sample playback rate with a synth oscillator.
arrangement_moves: hold a tonic-like anchor under changing harmony
use rhythmic gaps to let the kick breathe
remove sub during a solo or transition to create contrast
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Oscillator availability and slider support still belong to the active embedded runtime contract.

instrument_palettes.name: Synth Bass Groove
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create a distinct rhythmic and melodic fingerprint that locks with or deliberately contrasts the kick. Let rests, note lengths, and register define articulation.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use a documented waveform source such as `sawtooth`, `square`, `triangle`, or `sine` when appropriate and supported. Keep exact filter/envelope methods aligned to the rules and avoid relying on an unverified preset name.
arrangement_moves: transform the same bass cell by rhythm or register
answer the lead in the gaps
switch between sustained anchor and syncopated phrase
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Source labels and control methods must match the pinned runtime.

instrument_palettes.name: Acid / Resonant Sequence
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Build a memorable repeating note cell and make timbral motion part of the musical phrasing. Resonance should color the groove rather than erase pitch clarity.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use a documented oscillator and supported low-pass/resonance controls. Do not assume a literal TB-303 preset, bank, or extension exists. Keep filter ranges sensible and every moving control tied to an actual supported value domain.
arrangement_moves: open the filter across phrases
mute one sequence step to change the groove's contour
let the sequence disappear while a new motif takes over
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Acid character is a design strategy, not a guarantee of a dedicated preset.

instrument_palettes.name: Pluck / Arpeggio / Sequenced Notes
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use a compact pitch vocabulary, carefully spaced events, and articulation contrast. Arpeggios should support harmony or a motif instead of becoming decorative motion without direction.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use `note(...)` or `n(...).scale(...)` with a documented oscillator or confirmed sample source. Keep note syntax and scale declarations valid; don't assume a string named `pluck` exists.
arrangement_moves: change accent position while keeping pitch identity
stretch the motif into a slower phrase
move the sequence into a contrasting register
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Any custom pluck sound name must be confirmed in the runtime's sound map.

instrument_palettes.name: Lead Synth / Main Motif
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Own the central melodic identity. Vary phrase endings, register, rhythm, and timbre so the lead can carry both recognition and development.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use a verified pitched oscillator or sound source. `sawtooth`, `triangle`, `square`, and `sine` are familiar oscillator choices in documented contexts; `supersaw` is runtime-dependent and should be fallback-safe.
arrangement_moves: introduce a small motif then expand its phrase length
give the solo a question-answer shape
bring the opening idea back in transformed register or rhythm
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Do not assume every oscillator or visualizer hook is enabled in the pinned embedding.

instrument_palettes.name: Piano / Rhodes-Like Keys
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use voicing, register, note duration, and silence to create an expressive harmonic center. Avoid overfilling every subdivision with chords.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: A source literally named `piano` is sample-map dependent; use it only when confirmed. A verified oscillator can provide a dependable fallback, while keeping the role and phrase intact.
arrangement_moves: alternate shell voicings with fuller chords
let the left hand imply harmony while the lead has space
strip the drums and expose chord color
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Piano/Rhodes sample availability is runtime-map dependent; do not assert a sample exists without evidence.

instrument_palettes.name: FM Bell / Glass / Metallic Melody
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create bright, sparse transients or resonant melodic signatures. Keep them separated from busy cymbals and let decay and spacing carry the atmosphere.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Documented FM controls may be used only when confirmed in the target runtime; otherwise use a verified `sine` or `triangle` source with conservative pitch and envelope choices. Custom mallet sample names are map-dependent.
arrangement_moves: use a short two- or three-note signature
move accents against the drum grid
turn the bell motif into a distant callback
instrument_palettes.compatibility: FM/operator variants are version-sensitive; keep an oscillator fallback.

instrument_palettes.name: Warm / Wide Harmonic Pad
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Hold harmonic color and emotional continuity. Use long values, clear voice-leading, and breathing room; change voicing or harmony meaningfully rather than simply raising the number of layers.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use a verified sustained synth source and documented supported effects. Avoid assuming a sample called `pad` is loaded. Manage long tails and orbit sharing carefully.
arrangement_moves: let one chord linger through percussion changes
invert or thin a voicing when the lead enters
shift from harmonic support into an exposed drone
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Pad presets and sample names are map-dependent; oscillator construction is a fallback.

instrument_palettes.name: Drone / Harmonic Sculpture
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create a slowly changing environment from stable tones, small pitch shifts, or layered partial roles. A drone can evolve through filtering, register, and entrances without conventional chord changes.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Prefer a verified sustained oscillator and conservative filtering. A drone is not a reason to introduce custom audio nodes or unverified continuous modulation calls.
arrangement_moves: change only one spectral layer at a time
let the drone remain while a sparse motif appears
remove harmonics for a long quiet center
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Keep long release and feedback choices conservative; verify continuous modulation support.

instrument_palettes.name: Strings / Orchestral Sustains
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Build sustained harmony, counterpoint, or ostinato patterns. Use register separation and clear voice-leading to avoid turning strings into an undifferentiated midrange block.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Orchestral sample names are dependent on the active map. When unavailable, preserve the part's melodic role with a verified oscillator or simplify the line rather than inventing string presets.
arrangement_moves: introduce one voice before the ensemble
convert sustained lines into a repeated ostinato
use contrary motion around the main motif
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Specific orchestral sample sources require confirmation in the REPL sound browser.

instrument_palettes.name: Choir / Wordless Vocal Texture
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create the impression of a vocal ensemble through held chord shapes, call-and-response, or syllabic rhythmic gestures. Do not invent lyrics unless requested.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Choir and vocal sample/preset names are not guaranteed. Use only confirmed sources; an oscillator pad can serve as a fallback for the harmonic role without pretending it is an actual choir sample.
arrangement_moves: answer a lead with a short choral phrase
bring voices in only at structural peaks
fragment the harmony into distant single-note responses
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Voice libraries are sample-map dependent; avoid unverified named sources.

instrument_palettes.name: Guitar / Plucked String Texture
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use plucked phrasing, open intervals, repeated picking cells, or harmonic accents. Keep attacks distinct and avoid pretending an oscillator is a sampled guitar when realism matters.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use guitar samples only after checking the sound map. For a robust fallback, compose the same part as a sparse note pattern on a verified oscillator and label it as a synth interpretation, not a guitar sample.
arrangement_moves: transform a picking cell into a pad-like slower phrase
use an exposed plucked motif between heavier sections
let a repeated pulse support an evolving top line
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Guitar source names are sample-map dependent.

instrument_palettes.name: Breakbeat / Chopped Percussion
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Give the composition forward motion through syncopation, gaps, and phrase-level accent changes. Preserve a recognizable rhythmic source rather than applying random slicing everywhere.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use confirmed drum samples or default-map percussion patterns. Chopping/slicing methods should be used only with documented signatures and appropriate source material; do not depend on an `amen` or named break sample unless it is loaded.
arrangement_moves: alternate tightly controlled and fragmented phrases
strip the break down to a few transient anchors
reassemble fragments into a clearer groove at the climax
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Named break samples and advanced slicing are dependent on loaded assets and runtime support.

instrument_palettes.name: Noise / Foley / Transition Effects
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use noise and short effects to mark space, transitions, or texture. They should clarify a transition or narrative detail, not mask the rhythmic core.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use documented noise source types or sample names only when supported. Avoid inventing `riser`, `impact`, or `whoosh` sample names. Build transition intent with existing confirmed sounds when possible.
arrangement_moves: use a brief noise swell at a section boundary
remove effects during a motif spotlight
turn a repeated effect rhythm into a percussive voice
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Foley and effect samples require a real loaded sample map.

instrument_palettes.name: Atmosphere / Field-Recording Bed
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create a sense of place and depth while leaving headroom for pitched and rhythmic material. Treat environmental sound as a structural layer with entrances, exits, and changes of focus.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: External recordings are not implicitly available. Use a confirmed sample or a restrained documented noise source; don't fetch remote audio or invent URLs in generated scores.
arrangement_moves: expose atmosphere before rhythm arrives
thin the music until the environmental layer becomes foreground
reuse a tiny texture as an identity anchor at the ending
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Field recordings require user-supplied or loaded audio assets; no automatic network loading is assumed.

instrument_palettes.name: Orchestral Impact / Brass-Style Accent
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use sparse, coordinated accents to punctuate transitions and harmonic changes. Reserve impact for meaningful events; continuous impacts lose their dramatic function.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Brass/orchestral sample names are map-dependent. Use only confirmed sounds; a coordinated chord stab on a verified oscillator can preserve the rhythmic/harmonic function.
arrangement_moves: mark movement boundaries with a single accent
answer a lead phrase with ensemble stabs
hold the biggest impact for a later arrival
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Specific orchestral patches require an available sample/preset map.

instrument_palettes.name: Chiptune / 8-bit Pulse
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use limited waveforms, clear arpeggiated harmony, purposeful octave shifts, and short motifs. The limited palette should become an identity rather than a constraint that causes monotony.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use verified `square`, `triangle`, or pulse-like sources where supported. Avoid assuming an NES/chip preset or special sound bank is loaded.
arrangement_moves: turn a motif into an arpeggiated harmony
shift bass and lead by octave rather than adding timbral layers
use a slower bridge with the same pitch vocabulary
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Pulse/triangle sources are runtime-dependent; confirm accepted synth names.

instrument_palettes.name: Organ / Sustained Chord Stabs
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use chordal attacks as rhythmic punctuation or warm sustained harmony. Let the bass and percussion own their own space; avoid placing every chord at the same density.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Organ-like samples or presets are map-dependent. Use confirmed sources or a simple oscillator approximation when necessary; use voicing and note length to carry the role.
arrangement_moves: alternate short stabs and held chords
use call-and-response with lead
strip harmony to a single note during a breakdown
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Named organ sounds must be checked in the active REPL.

instrument_palettes.name: Brass / Reed / Bold Midrange
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create a human-like call, sustained counterline, or bold accent through contour and timing. Distinguish a unison hook from chordal support and avoid crowding lead vocals or synth leads.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Specific brass/reed samples are map-dependent. Don't claim a synth oscillator sounds like a trumpet; use confirmed samples or preserve the musical role with a clear synth line.
arrangement_moves: write a short response phrase after the lead
save fuller chord stabs for peaks
thin to one reed-like line in a transition
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Instrument realism depends on the sound map and available samples.

instrument_palettes.name: Mallets / Marimba / Xylophone / Kalimba Roles
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use short repeating cells with a clear pitch contour and acoustic-like spacing. Let rhythmic repetition support gentle variation instead of overdecorating the pattern.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Named mallet samples are map-dependent. If unavailable, use a verified simple waveform with short articulation and sparse notes rather than referencing imaginary presets.
arrangement_moves: interlock two short note cells
move the melody into a different register
strip accompaniment until the mallet motif stands alone
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Sample-based mallet sources require sound-map confirmation.

instrument_palettes.name: Rhythmic Texture / Non-pitched Pulse
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Use short events, controlled density, and rests to create motion without demanding melodic attention. Make texture support the groove or the narrative.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Prefer confirmed default-map percussion/noise sources. Keep all exotic sources optional and verify their existence before relying on them.
arrangement_moves: move the texture from background to foreground
reduce the pattern to sparse transients
let different accents imply a new meter while the pulse stays stable
instrument_palettes.compatibility: The chosen sound source must be present in the sound map.

instrument_palettes.name: Minimal Piano / Exposed Harmony
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Build emotion from motif spacing, register, repetition, and small changes in harmony. Silence is part of the arrangement; resist automatic percussion or a cinematic crescendo unless requested.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use a confirmed piano sample or a verified oscillator fallback. Keep one audible line or a clear voice-leading structure instead of stacking unrelated phrases.
arrangement_moves: repeat a phrase with one changed note
move from open voicing to a closer voicing
leave a long breath between motifs
instrument_palettes.compatibility: The piano sample itself requires map confirmation.

instrument_palettes.name: Counterline / Small Ensemble
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Give independent voices distinct registers and different phrase lengths while preserving a shared harmonic or rhythmic relationship. If two layers compete, change their timing or register rather than only lowering gain.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use simple verified sources, named note patterns, and `stack(...)` when supported. Keep every voice connected to the final root and avoid relying on unverified orchestral presets.
arrangement_moves: introduce voices one at a time
let one voice complete the other's phrase
remove voices and bring them back in altered order
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Ensemble behavior comes from pattern relationships; timbral realism is source-dependent.

instrument_palettes.name: Glitch / Granular-Like Fragmentation
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Create controlled fragmentation with small event groups, cutoffs, repeats, and omissions while keeping a recurring motif or pulse identifiable. Distinguish deliberate fragmentation from malformed code.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use documented conditional/time transformations and confirmed source material. Granular-specific or buffer operations are extension-dependent unless explicitly present in the runtime rules.
arrangement_moves: fracture a motif during one section only
reassemble fragments into a coherent phrase
leave a clean unprocessed return after the noisy passage
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Granular engine functions are not assumed to exist in core Strudel.

instrument_palettes.name: Formant / Synthetic Choir Color
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Suggest vowels or vocal-like motion through supported tonal/filter choices without promising speech synthesis. Use distinct phrase timing so the layer reads as a voice-like motif rather than a static chord.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Only use documented and runtime-supported vowel/formant controls and verified source names. If uncertain, use a plain supported oscillator and skip specialized formant methods.
arrangement_moves: use a repeated vowel-like contour as a signature
move from a drone to syllabic rhythmic fragments
contrast a narrow and broad register
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Exact vowel/formant support depends on the pinned runtime and source.

instrument_palettes.name: Noise Transient / Shaker / Brush Roles
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Add fine-grained pulse and tactile motion with modest gain. Let transient density respond to the arrangement; low-level noise should not become a constant masking layer.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use confirmed percussion aliases or supported `white`, `pink`, or `brown` noise sources as documented. Don't invent brushes or shaker samples.
arrangement_moves: bring in fine texture after the main groove settles
make transient density the main build variable
remove noise during the motif spotlight
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Noise source support and sample aliases must be checked in target runtime.

instrument_palettes.name: Harmonic Bass / Root Motion
instrument_palettes.role_guidance: Make the bass articulate harmonic turns and support the chord rhythm. It can hold roots, move through passing notes, or use an ostinato that intentionally delays harmonic resolution.
instrument_palettes.source_guidance: Use verified note or scale-degree patterns, a supported source, and simple filter/gain controls. Do not infer key from genre or force a scale when the brief seeks atonality.
arrangement_moves: change root movement under a fixed motif
suspend the bass before harmonic arrival
share one rhythmic cell between bass and lead at different pitches
instrument_palettes.compatibility: Tonal analysis from source code can be approximate; explicit user key/mode instructions take precedence.

visual_palettes.name: Inline Punchcard / Transformed Event Map
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Show timing, accents, omissions, and transformed event placement for rhythmic or otherwise event-dense patterns.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Attach after event transformations when the transformed result is what should be inspected. Add `.color(...)` deliberately if distinct colors improve readability.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Inline Pianoroll / Pitch-Time Map
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Show pitch register, note duration, and phrase relationships for pitched patterns.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Attach to a pattern that carries the relevant note data. The documented pianoroll visualizes the pattern at its position; use punchcard instead when later transformations should be visible.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Oscilloscope / Time-Domain Scope
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Inspect waveform behavior, transient shape, amplitude movement, and periodic oscillation. It is diagnostic, not a sound-quality verdict.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Attach to the audio-bearing pattern whose waveform matters. Keep any scope options limited to documented fields.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Spectrum Analyzer / Frequency Balance
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Inspect relative spectral energy and broad timbral changes, especially when filters or layers change over time.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Attach to an appropriate sound-bearing pattern and avoid treating the display as a mix meter for the entire composition unless the REPL actually aggregates it.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Spiral / Cycle Geometry
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Explore cycle-related timing, repeated movement, and layered periodicity as a visual metaphor.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Use on a pattern with a meaningful cycle; avoid implying the spiral proves harmonic or rhythmic correctness.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Pitchwheel / Pitch-Class Circle
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Visualize pitch/frequency relationships within an octave, especially for tonal material or pitch-class motion.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Use where the pattern contains interpretable pitch data; it is less informative for pure percussion or unpitched noise.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Mini-Notation Color / Active-Event Highlighting
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Use color to make active mini-notation events and pattern identity easier to inspect; color is visual feedback, not audio processing.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Use named or CSS colors documented by the REPL. Chain placement matters for some visualizers; color applied after `_punchcard()` can still affect punchcard feedback, while color after `_pianoroll()` may not.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Global / Background Pianoroll or Punchcard
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Provide a page-level view or aggregate feedback when the host supports global rendering.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Global visuals may contend with inline visualizations and depend on host/editor support. Use only when available; inline `_...()` variants are better when multiple specific layers need their own view.

visual_palettes.name: Hydra Generative Visual Layer
visual_palettes.visual_call: Hydra integration such as `initHydra()` and `H(...)` only in an explicitly enabled compatible host
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Offer an optional generative visual engine for users explicitly asking for Hydra or an audio-reactive visual performance.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: EXPERIMENTAL / EXTENSION-ONLY. Do not auto-inject Hydra setup into ordinary pattern-only scores. It needs compatible host support and may alter the single-root/output assumptions.
visual_palettes.verification_status: official docs describe the integration; not guaranteed in MotifAI's embedded REPL

visual_palettes.name: Multi-View Visual Direction
visual_palettes.visual_call: Use a restrained mix of `._punchcard()`, `._pianoroll()`, `._scope()`, `._spectrum()`, `._spiral()`, and `._pitchwheel()` where supported.
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Select complementary displays for different audible roles rather than adding every display to every stem.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Usually use one visual per representative role and a small total count. Keep visual hooks optional, attach them after the intended data-generating/transform stage, and remove a failing visual hook without deleting its musical pattern.
visual_palettes.verification_status: selection strategy built from officially documented visuals; each embedded hook still runtime-dependent

visual_palettes.name: Pianoroll Detail / Labels and Register Window
visual_palettes.visual_call: `._pianoroll({ labels: 1 })` using documented options where supported
visual_palettes.when_to_use: Add readable note labels or focus the display on a meaningful pitch range when inspection matters.
visual_palettes.placement_guidance: Use only documented option fields; avoid visual overconfiguration if the default view is readable.
visual_palettes.verification_status: officially documented options; embedded availability remains runtime-dependent

production_palettes.name: Low-End Role Separation
production_palettes.principle: Give kick transients and bass sustain or rhythm different jobs; create gaps before adding more compression or layers.
moves: separate register and timing
reduce bass activity during kick accents
keep sub movement sparse under dense harmony
production_palettes.caveat: No mix is validated by source inspection; audition the result.

production_palettes.name: Groove Pocket and Swing
production_palettes.principle: Establish the rhythmic fingerprint with a few complementary parts before increasing subdivision density.
moves: vary accents rather than adding layers
let kick and bass answer one another
use rests as syncopation
production_palettes.caveat: Timing transformations are cycle-based and method-specific; verify their exact semantics.

production_palettes.name: Motif Transformation
production_palettes.principle: Keep the identity recognizable while changing one or two dimensions at a time: rhythm, contour, register, harmony, timbre, or phrase length.
moves: fragment then recombine
invert or relocate a phrase when musically appropriate
bring back an opening idea with a changed role
production_palettes.caveat: Do not declare evolution just because a variable name or effect value changed.

production_palettes.name: Harmonic Space and Voice Leading
production_palettes.principle: Use spacing, register, and phrase length to keep the tonal center legible or intentionally destabilize it. Treat inferred scale information as a hint, not a command.
moves: thin voicings under busy leads
hold one common tone through a chord shift
use modal mixture only when it serves the brief
production_palettes.caveat: Harmony may be tonal, modal, chromatic, or atonal according to intent.

production_palettes.name: Density and Arrangement Headroom
production_palettes.principle: Create contrast through entrances and omissions, not only through adding more tracks.
moves: remove one layer before a major entrance
reduce event rate while keeping the pulse
rotate the foreground role between stems
production_palettes.caveat: Every layer should have a distinct function and remain connected to the final root.

production_palettes.name: Tension, Release, and Payoff
production_palettes.principle: Build anticipation using controlled changes in density, register, rhythm, filtering, or harmonic instability, then make the release clearly different.
moves: create a brief gap
change the bass/lead relationship at the peak
return to a familiar motif after the impact
production_palettes.caveat: Not every piece needs a drop or climax.

production_palettes.name: Delay / Reverb Space Hygiene
production_palettes.principle: Treat reverb and delay as shared orbit resources; avoid conflicting per-pattern settings on stems that share one orbit.
moves: keep dry transients readable
assign distinct orbit numbers when distinct sends are needed and supported
reduce tails during dense sections
production_palettes.caveat: The embedded runtime must confirm orbit routing and supported effect names.

production_palettes.name: Timbre as Section Identity
production_palettes.principle: Use a few contrasting source/processing identities tied to structural roles; avoid changing timbre on every stem at once.
moves: change one source family while retaining motif
use filtering as a transition, not a substitute for development
introduce one contrasting register or attack
production_palettes.caveat: Every named source and method must be present in the target runtime.

production_palettes.name: Long-Form Continuity and Movement Memory
production_palettes.principle: Make each movement distinct while retaining a few shared identity anchors, recurring motifs, rhythmic relatives, or transition materials.
moves: recontextualize a motif
use a shared tone or rhythm across movement boundaries
allow energy to fall intentionally between peaks
production_palettes.caveat: Concert duration needs real cycle-rate and arrangement-unit calculations; do not invent bar counts.

production_palettes.name: Controlled Generative Variation
production_palettes.principle: Keep transformations related to the musical identity and use conditional/time modifiers deliberately, rather than randomizing every layer independently.
moves: vary a phrase every few cycles
use call-and-response across stable pulse layers
freeze one motif while another varies
production_palettes.caveat: Advanced helper semantics must be confirmed for the pinned version.

production_palettes.name: Minimalism and Negative Space
production_palettes.principle: Make every sound count; space and repetition carry structure. Don't expand into a climax by default.
moves: introduce one voice at a time
repeat a phrase with one small change
leave empty cycles or gaps where musical timing permits
production_palettes.caveat: A small score can be more intentional than a large one.

production_palettes.name: Section Transition Craft
production_palettes.principle: A transition should prepare the next idea while preserving the current pulse or giving a deliberate reason to break it.
moves: use an outgoing motif fragment
strip the bass before a new harmonic arrival
change texture over a shared pulse
production_palettes.caveat: Use only the arrangement construction method confirmed in MotifAI's runtime contract.

production_palettes.name: Visual Feedback Paired to Audible Function
production_palettes.principle: A visual should reveal the property of the pattern it is attached to: pitch-time, event density, waveform, spectrum, cycle relationship, or pitch class.
moves: punchcard for transformed event timing
pianoroll for pitched note placement
scope/spectrum for signal behavior
spiral/pitchwheel for cycle or pitch-class views
production_palettes.caveat: Visual hooks are optional and runtime-dependent; never treat a display as proof of sound quality.
